column1: # Shared JSON-escape test vectors for __gpy_escape_json (bash/zsh) and
# pair per line. Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored.
# `input` uses a mini escape scheme to carry bytes a TSV row cannot hold
# literally -- backslash first, then control chars: \\ -> one literal
# tab. Every reading test MUST unescape `input` the same way (backslash
# first) before calling the shell's escape function under test.
# unescaping) must turn into -- i.e. exactly what the escape function's
# stdout should be -- and needs NO further processing: a correct
# implementation already emits \\, \n, \r, \t as literal two-character
# sequences, which is what appears here. (A one-backslash input's `input`
# and `expected` columns can look identical on disk -- e.g. `a\\b` for
# both -- because the mini escape scheme for a literal backslash happens
# to coincide with JSON's own backslash-escaping. That is not a mistake.)
